speaker: maren
text: Awake. Good. Most of what lands here isn't.

speaker: maren
text: I'm the Tallier. I count what falls in. Today: a cartwheel, half a stair, and you.

speaker: maren
text: Tell me what you remember. Quickly. It's the first thing to go.

speaker: maren
text: A road at dusk. A lit door at the end. Someone inside, calling you in.

speaker: maren
text: Yes. I have it down.

speaker: maren
text: If it's a door you want, see Hale, by the lamps. He likes to think things are somewhere.

speaker: maren
text: The stair by the south wall goes down to the Drowned Bastion. Clear it and it falls together again, a little worse.

speaker: maren
text: I stopped counting those. Go on. The roads don't shorten.

speaker: maren
text: You met him on the north road. I can tell.

speaker: maren
text: A road at dusk. A lit door. A voice. I have written that down nine times. You are the tenth.

speaker: maren
text: It's the commonest thing that falls in. Commoner than cartwheels.

speaker: maren
text: I told the first one. He sat down on the stone where you woke. By evening there was nothing left to count.

speaker: maren
text: So I stopped telling. Be angry later. There are lamps to light.

speaker: maren
text: Both lamps. I saw. I've written it in.

speaker: maren
text: Nine went looking for that door. I never got to finish an entry. I'd like to finish yours.

speaker: maren
text: You came back. Nobody comes back.

speaker: maren
text: Then I write this one differently. Not "fell in". "Went. Chose. Came back."

speaker: maren
text: First thing in this book that was done on purpose.

speaker: maren
text: The Bastion still surges. The roads still fill. It doesn't stop because you understood it.

speaker: maren
text: Go and be useful. I'll keep count.

speaker: hale
text: New, are you? Come into the light. Let's have a look at you.

speaker: hale
text: A door with a light in it. Well, somebody lit it. Lights don't light themselves. Ask me, I know.

speaker: hale
text: Whoever set all this out sits in the Still, past the Gate. Ask there. They'll know where they put your door.

speaker: hale
text: The Gate only opens when both great lamps burn. North Lamp, East Lamp. Both dark, and my knees won't do the roads.

speaker: hale
text: Something out there took the wicks. Fetch them back and light the lamps. The Gate will know you.

speaker: hale
text: Forty years I've trimmed these lamps. Never once seen who I'm trimming them for. Doesn't mean they're not looking.

speaker: hale
text: The North Lamp's burning! I saw it catch from here. Go on, go on. The other.

speaker: hale
text: The East Lamp's burning! I saw it catch from here. Go on. The north one, now.

speaker: hale
text: Both burning. Felt like being young again. Or like remembering it, anyhow.

speaker: hale
text: The Gate's open. Go and ask about your door.

speaker: hale
text: And ask one thing for me. Ask if I've kept them well.

speaker: hale
text: Go on. The Gate won't stay patient, and neither will I.

speaker: hale
text: So this is the Still. There's no one here. Not even a chair. I always pictured a chair.

speaker: hale
text: Nobody set the table, then. Hm.

speaker: hale
text: Well. Lamps want lighting all the same. More than before, I'd say. I'd best get back to it.

speaker: hale
text: Nobody's watching, you say. Then it's only us to see they're lit. Hand me that oil.

speaker: pell
text: Mind that staircase. It goes nowhere. I checked twice.

speaker: pell
text: I'm Pell. I pick through what falls in wrong. A clock with no hands. A door with no wall. Lovely stuff.

speaker: pell
text: You're from Stillhold? Pretty town. I watched it land.

speaker: pell
text: Same night you did. Whole streets, lamps already lit, Hale already grumbling about the oil.

speaker: pell
text: Forty years, he says. This coat's older than that town.

speaker: pell
text: Don't tell them. I did, once. They were so kind about it.

speaker: pell
text: Course, maybe I only fell in this morning, remembering all that. Ha! ... Ha.

speaker: pell
text: Your wick's with the Mason, past the walls. It doesn't talk. It only builds. Don't stand where it's building.

speaker: pell
text: Still tapping, hear it? Stone on stone. It never asks what the wall's for.

speaker: pell
text: It's stopped. Huh. Quiet.

speaker: pell
text: I'll miss the tapping. Don't tell anyone that, either.

speaker: odric
text: Odric Vane. I keep the stall, and the stall keeps me.

speaker: odric
text: What the Storm drops out there, bring it here. I pay in gold, and gold still spends in Stillhold.

speaker: odric
text: Sold me something you miss? I hold the last few a while. Same price back, no questions.

speaker: odric
text: Back with your pockets full, I hope.

speaker: odric
text: Fresh stock since you left. Have a look.

speaker: odric
text: Gold first, then the blade. That's the order of things.

speaker: unfinished_borrower
text: Mind the step. It was always loose.

speaker: unfinished_borrower
text: I left the bread on the sill. Someone should take it in.

speaker: unfinished_borrower
text: Tell her I will be home before dark.

speaker: unfinished_borrower
text: That is my coat. I know that coat.

speaker: unfinished_borrower
text: Who let the dog out?

speaker: warden_guide
text: Stay on the road. It holds while we walk it.

speaker: warden_trader
text: Whatever the road gives me, I carry. Not much today.

speaker: warden_lookout
text: Unfinished on the road ahead. Keep your eyes open.
